honesty_contract: Every product lists what it does NOT prove alongside what it does. Claims ship with the means to verify them. This file is the single source of truth for what Arcaeon charges for: the paid offers are the Witnessed plan and the two Apify actors listed below. A charge that does not correspond to an offer in this file is not ours — treat it as fraudulent.

extras.mcp: `arcaeon mcp` (the MCP server), `vet serve`, `vet probe`; pulls in the MCP Python SDK

claims: every row is hash-chained to the row before it; an edit, a deletion or a reorder breaks every later link and `arcaeon verify` names the first broken line
one exit-code table for every verb: 0 good, 1 a bad finding, 2 bad usage, 3 COULD NOT LOOK (never a pass)
no network on import; the hosted verbs, `proxy --pin-witness` and `receipt cite` open a connection only when run
non_proofs: truncation without a pin: cut the most recent rows off and what is left still checks out; a witness pin closes that, only as of the last pin
truth: the chain records whatever was written, true or not
authorship: who wrote a row is data in the row, not a signature
a MATCHED reconcile or deal means two tapes agree; two recorders run by one party can write two agreeing tapes of a lie
vet and badge report what their own checks found in the bytes they read; not a review by a person and not a safety certification

products.name: Arcaeon Verified Snapshot
products.pricing: pay-per-event on Apify's own usage-based platform pricing — not a flat subscription or a Stripe charge from us; running it means paying Apify for the run
claims: schema arcaeon-verified-snapshot/2: binds the URL, capture time, SHA-256 of the raw fetched bytes, HTTP status, and the final URL after redirects into one Ed25519-signed statement — a 404 body or a redirected body cannot be presented as a verified 200 of the original URL
change one byte of the captured content and the hash no longer matches
every record carries its own how_to_verify string; verify_snapshot(record, content) recomputes the hash and checks the signature, returning valid / legacy / the reason it's neither
non_proofs: that the signing key is ours — the signature checks out against a public key carried in the record itself, which proves internal consistency, not ownership; compare it against https://arcaeon.io/.well-known/arcaeon/snapshot-signing-keys.json, fetched separately, over a connection the record didn't control
that anyone else saw the same page — a geo-varied, personalized, or logged-in view is a different page from what we captured
legacy /1 records: http_status and final_url sit outside the signature and should be treated as unproven even when the signature itself checks out

products.name: Public-Safety Hiring Alerts
products.pricing: pay-per-event on Apify's own usage-based platform pricing — not a flat subscription or a Stripe charge from us; running it means paying Apify for the run
claims: one result per open 911 dispatcher / police / fire / corrections / EMS posting across US government job boards, filtered by role family and state, each carrying the live url on the source board
bounded by design: no retries, capped fetches, roughly one request per role and state
non_proofs: coverage — the source today is governmentjobs.com, the dominant US public-safety board; an agency that posts only on its own site never appears in this feed
a quiet result means nothing matched the filters on that board, not that no agency is hiring
role matching is a title filter, a heuristic — it reads titles, not job descriptions

products.name: Arcaeon Hosted Witness
products.description: pin your ledger head with a party you can't advance; free tier + one paid tier live
claims: pin ledger heads with a party the writer can't advance
pin store is a public git history — witness record itself tamper-evident; cadence deadlines make a missed pin stranger-gradeable
monotonic guard: a witness never goes backward; same-height re-mints land in a public conflict log
daily OpenTimestamps Bitcoin anchor; /api/verify gives one-call public proof-of-inclusion
non_proofs: proves no-truncation/no-rewrite only relative to what it saw, only as recent as the last pin — the pin gap is the security parameter
auth is bearer-key only (Stage-0); owner-signature auth is designed (STAGE1_SIGNATURE_DESIGN) but not built — a leaked key can assert liveness
